keyChanges.title: Q2 paid miles actually fell 36% QoQ — hot context understated the decline
keyChanges.description: Multiple credible sources including TechCrunch (July 23) and Tesla's own Q2 cumulative-miles chart confirm that Tesla Robotaxi paid miles fell approximately 36% quarter-over-quarter: Q1 2026 was roughly 1.1 million paid miles, Q2 2026 was roughly 700,000 — not 'flat' at ~900k as framed in Q2 materials. The prior week's hot context accepted Tesla's cumulative 2.4M figure and derived ~900k Q2 by differencing; multiple outlets now show Tesla's own per-quarter disclosure puts Q1 higher (~1.1M) and Q2 lower (~700k). Tesla's explanation is that the company deliberately redirected Model Y robotaxi miles toward Cybercab-specific data collection. Analysts and investors have not accepted that framing — TSLA fell ~14.5% post-earnings in part on this data. The active unsupervised fleet remains approximately 21 vehicles after ~14 months of paid commercial service. Phoenix and Las Vegas were listed in the Q2 letter as 'preparations underway' — no confirmed launch in this period.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: Tesla's own figures, now properly read quarter-to-quarter, show a 36% decline in paid miles — not growth and not flat. The safety/data-collection narrative is a rationalization, not a plan. Fleet has not grown in 14 months.

positive_signals: Cumulative 2.4M paid miles is a real number and continues to grow
Tesla claims 0 notable incidents across 380k+ unsupervised miles
Q2 shareholder letter lists Phoenix and Las Vegas as 'preparations underway' — expansion pipeline exists
negative_signals: Q2 paid miles ~700k vs Q1 ~1.1M = -36% QoQ, per Tesla's own chart per TechCrunch analysis
Active unsupervised fleet still ~21 vehicles after 14+ months of paid service — no fleet growth
TSLA fell ~14.5% post-earnings in part on robotaxi stall narrative
Phoenix and Las Vegas did not launch in H1 2026 as originally promised — now 'preparations underway' with no new date
Tesla's explanation (data collection for Cybercab) is unverified and not a recovery plan
Waymo still orders of magnitude ahead on weekly driverless paid miles
Cybercab still not generating a single paid commercial mile

key_metrics.actual: ~700k paid miles Q2 (down from ~1.1M Q1); cumulative 2.4M; fleet ~21 unsupervised vehicles
key_metrics.target: Scale to hundreds of vehicles per city; competitive with Waymo weekly mile count
key_metrics.trajectory: Declining QoQ paid miles; geographic expansion without utilization growth = compounding failure

keyChanges.title: Tesla quietly removes 'volume production in 2026' language for Cybercab from Q2 shareholder letter
keyChanges.description: In its Q2 2026 shareholder letter (July 22, widely reported July 23), Tesla removed explicit 'volume production in 2026' commitments for the Cybercab, Tesla Semi, and Megapack 3 — language that was present as recently as the Q1 2026 letter. TechCrunch's analysis of the letter diff confirmed the deletion. Tesla's new language describes Cybercab as being in 'start of production' with volume dependent on scaling 4680 battery cell output. The company said it is working to increase 4680 production to support Cybercab and Semi at scale. No replacement timeline was provided. This is the second time Tesla has silently walked back a Cybercab production milestone: the original June 2025 'before end of year' public launch slipped, and now 2026 volume production has been dropped without acknowledgment. The Cybercab at this date has 245 units staged at Giga Texas, zero in paid fleet service, and is in an on-campus employee ride phase plus on-road engineering test phase in Austin.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: Silent removal of volume production timeline is a material negative. Production is real but 'volume' in 2026 is now off the table per Tesla's own letter. No new timeline given.

245 staged Cybercabs = ~0.7 days of claimed 125k annual capacity; inventory not deploying

key_metrics.actual: Cybercab in 'start of production'; ~245 units staged at Giga Texas; 0 in revenue service
key_metrics.trajectory: Production ramping slowly; volume target deferred to unknown future date; 4680 ramp is gating factor

keyChanges.title: Cybercabs appear in Charlotte, NC — 14 units with Texas plates, AI Safety Operator job posted
keyChanges.description: On July 25-27, 2026, observer reports and Axios Charlotte confirmed 14 Tesla Cybercabs and 14 Model Y vehicles bearing Texas plates in a Charlotte-area parking lot — the first confirmed out-of-state Cybercab deployment destination from the Giga Texas staging inventory. Tesla simultaneously posted an AI Safety Operator job for Charlotte to 'oversee daily operations of ride-hailing services' and collect data by driving in a 'designated area' for 6-8 hours per day. This mirrors the exact playbook Tesla ran before every prior robotaxi market launch: vehicle pre-positioning followed by safety-operator-supervised data-collection rides before unsupervised public service. Charlotte is not a launched market — it is the earliest pre-launch data-collection phase. Waymo has also been testing in Charlotte for months, setting up a potential direct competitive confrontation. The key read: Charlotte's appearance is the first evidence that Cybercabs are physically leaving Giga Texas for operational staging, which is required before any paid service — but it is phase zero of a multi-phase process that took Austin roughly 12 months from vehicle arrival to unsupervised paid rides.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Cybercabs physically leaving Texas for a new city is a real operational step. But the pattern from every prior market shows 6-12 months between vehicle arrival and paid unsupervised service. Charlotte is in data-collection phase zero.

No permit filing or ride-hailing license confirmed for Charlotte yet

key_metrics.target: Paid unsupervised Cybercab service in Charlotte
key_metrics.trajectory: Phase 0 pre-launch data collection; paid service likely 6-12+ months away based on prior city timelines

keyChanges.title: Reuters: Tesla pressured EU regulators to seal FSD safety data before October bloc-wide vote
keyChanges.description: A Reuters investigation published August 6, 2026, based on emails obtained via Dutch public-records request, reveals that Tesla conditioned its cooperation with the Netherlands' RDW type-approval process on guarantees that safety evaluation documents would never be released publicly. The emails show Tesla began pressing RDW to keep FSD review documentation permanently sealed as early as late 2024. The Dutch regulator honored the demand: it will not disclose how it evaluated the technology, what test protocols were used, or what performance thresholds were required, despite RDW's subsequent push for EU-wide recognition of that same sealed approval. Separately, regulators in six EU countries including Germany, Norway, and Denmark told Reuters they cannot release FSD testing or performance data either, citing Tesla's trade-secret claims. A prior Reuters investigation in May 2026 found that Tesla's own published FSD safety statistics are significantly inflated — the company counted only severe crashes for its own fleet while using broader figures for overall crash rates, and assumed 100% fleet replacement by FSD-equipped Teslas to inflate lives-saved projections. The October 6 TCMV vote would authorize a type approval for all 27 EU member states based on a safety case that no member of the European public — and no non-approving regulator — has been permitted to see. The European Transport Safety Council (ETSC), which wrote to EU transport ministers on June 30, 2026 following a fatal Texas FSD crash, has urged ministers to withhold recognition until safety data is independently verified publicly.

positive_signals: RDW states it ran its own closed-track and public-road testing and did not rely solely on Tesla's inflated statistics
October 6 TCMV vote is now scheduled — a formal path to EU-wide recognition exists
negative_signals: Tesla emails show the company conditioned RDW cooperation on permanent confidentiality guarantees since late 2024
Six EU regulators (Germany, Norway, Denmark, and others) cannot release FSD testing data due to Tesla trade-secret claims
October 6 TCMV vote would ratify a safety case with no public transparency — no independent verification published

RDW's own stated confidence already retreated from 'safer than other ADAS' (April) to 'at least as safe' (June)
ETSC urging EU ministers to block recognition until safety data is verified — adds political friction ahead of October vote
France and Sweden are known TCMV opponents; data-secrecy revelations increase the chance other states join opposition

keyChanges.title: TCMV October 6 EU-wide FSD vote confirmed via German Ministry email; outcome far from certain
keyChanges.description: An official email from Germany's Federal Ministry of Transport, shared publicly around late July 2026, confirmed that the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) has a session scheduled for October 6, 2026, at which a vote on EU-wide approval of FSD (Supervised) is planned. If the vote achieves a qualified majority — at least 15 of 27 member states representing at least 65% of EU population — the European Commission would issue an implementing act authorizing the Dutch RDW approval to extend across all member states simultaneously. However, the outcome is highly uncertain: France's Transport Minister publicly rejected current FSD Supervised in late July, Sweden's transport authority has raised formal speed-offset objections to the TCMV, and the August 6 Reuters investigation into sealed safety data adds further political risk. Germany's KBA, which received a dedicated Tesla vehicle for independent evaluation in July 2026, has not reached a position. The ETSC has formally urged EU transport ministers to block recognition without public safety verification. A December vote or 2027 slip is explicitly flagged by multiple trackers if October fails. No new national approvals were granted in the July 23 - August 6 window; total consumer markets remain 6 (US + NL/LT/EE/DK/BE).

positive_signals: October 6 TCMV vote date now confirmed from official German Federal Ministry of Transport communication — formal EU-wide approval pathway is live
If passed, a single implementing act would unlock FSD across all 27 EU member states simultaneously
Germany is actively reviewing (test vehicle received July 2026) rather than flatly opposing
Finland's Traficom signaling possible pre-October national approval — could add a 7th consumer market

Sweden raised formal TCMV objections over speed offset; Finland, Norway, Denmark also have outstanding speed/icy-road questions
Reuters data-secrecy revelations raise political barrier for ministers who have not yet seen safety evidence
Qualified majority threshold (15 states + 65% population) is high — France alone accounts for ~15% EU population
October slot could slip to December or 2027 if any procedural objection delays the TCMV agenda
Major markets (Germany, France, Italy, Spain, UK) all still closed; 5 small-country footprint unchanged

keyChanges.title: Finland Traficom opens formal FSD review, signals possible approval before October EU vote
keyChanges.description: Finland's Transport and Communications Agency Traficom publicly stated it is assessing Tesla FSD (Supervised) for national type-approval recognition and is engaging directly with Tesla and other EU member state authorities. Traficom signaled it is prepared to move faster than the October 6 TCMV bloc-wide decision, provided Tesla resolves a handful of outstanding technical questions specific to Finnish operating conditions: (1) driver retake-of-control speed — how quickly drivers can assume control when FSD exits; (2) overtaking behavior in low-visibility conditions typical on Finnish rural roads; (3) the speed-offset feature that allows FSD to exceed posted limits to match traffic flow — the same issue Sweden and Norway have raised at TCMV level. If Traficom grants national recognition before October 6, Finland would become the 7th consumer market globally (6th in EU) for FSD Supervised. However, Traficom has not issued approval and all three technical questions remain open. Given Sweden's parallel TCMV objection on the same speed-offset issue, it is not clear Tesla has resolved the underlying regulatory concern that is also blocking the EU-wide vote.

positive_signals: Traficom officially opened formal review and is engaging with Tesla — Finland is on an active approval track, not a wait-and-see posture
Possibility of a 7th consumer market (6th EU) before October if Tesla answers technical questions
Traficom framed this as a technical gap-closing exercise, not a political rejection
Finland would add a Nordic market, expanding EU footprint beyond current Baltic/Benelux cluster
negative_signals: No approval granted yet — all three technical questions (retake speed, overtaking, speed offset) still open
Speed-offset concern mirrors Sweden's formal TCMV objection — Tesla has not publicly resolved this regulatory sticking point
Finland is a relatively small market (~5.5M population); approval here does not meaningfully advance the October EU vote math
Traficom has not committed to a timeline; 'ahead of October' is aspirational, not a deadline

keyChanges.title: FSD v14.3.6 regressions reported widely; Tesla responds with v14.3.7 (2026.21.5) OTA fix
keyChanges.description: Two distinct events bookend this research window. First, around July 28, Tesla Oracle and Teslarati documented owner reports of significant regressions in FSD v14.3.6 (2026.20.6.11): brake-stuttering / shadow-braking returned, with owners reporting unnecessary brake tapping, a blue tentacle constantly extending and retracting when confused by stationary pedestrians, left-lane camping, and highway-exit misses. The issues were notable enough to generate media coverage from multiple outlets even as Tesla continued widening the v14.3.6 rollout. Tesla responded by shipping FSD v14.3.7 in software package 2026.21.5, beginning rollout August 1. As of August 6, v14.3.7 was still in limited early-access distribution (less than 1% of HW4 fleet per TeslaFi). Release notes for v14.3.7 are nearly identical to v14.3.6 (same RL/MLIR/vision-encoder stack), but user reviews confirm the brake-stuttering regression is resolved; a highway-exit miss issue reportedly persists. Critical reality: Tesla shipping a regression-fix point-release within two weeks of a prior point-release is normal product cadence but signals ongoing instability in the v14.3.x branch at the very moment v15 robotaxi builds (still at ~40% completion) carry growing investor expectations. Consumer HW4 production software has now cycled v14.3.4 → v14.3.5 → v14.3.6 (regression) → v14.3.7 in roughly six weeks — incremental polish, not the architectural leap v15 represents.

positive_signals: Tesla responded quickly — v14.3.7 regression fix shipped approximately 10 days after v14.3.6 regressions were widely reported
v14.3.7 early-access users confirm brake-stuttering fixed; one reviewer noted zero instances of brake-stabbing, wheel-jerking, or unconfident movements
Rollout to early-access and influencer pool demonstrates active monitoring and fast iteration on v14.3.x branch
negative_signals: v14.3.6 introduced brake-stuttering / shadow-braking regression affecting multiple owners; Tesla Oracle and Teslarati documented complaints with video evidence
v14.3.7 release notes are nearly identical to v14.3.6 — no new capability, only regression patch; highway-exit miss reportedly still present
v14.3.7 still under 1% fleet rollout as of August 6 — most consumer HW4 owners remain on the regressed v14.3.6 build
Consumer production software remains on the v14.3.x branch — no v15 path visible in consumer OTA; v15 is fleet-only (robotaxi) at ~40% completion
Regression-then-patch cycle in v14.3.5 to v14.3.6 to v14.3.7 within six weeks signals instability as branch approaches its development ceiling

keyChanges.title: Ashok: Tesla permanently removing FSD max-speed offset; will learn implied speed preferences instead
keyChanges.description: During the research window, Tesla AI chief Ashok Elluswamy publicly confirmed that the manually configurable 'Max Speed' offset for FSD — which allowed drivers to set FSD to drive above posted speed limits — will not be reinstated. Ashok stated: 'Max speed control is an anti pattern' and confirmed Tesla is instead building systems that learn implied driver speed preferences from real behavior (e.g., when a driver taps the accelerator because FSD is too slow, the system logs and adapts). This was corroborated by Teslarati and NotATeslaApp. Context: Sweden and other EU regulators explicitly cited the manual speed offset toggle as a safety and compliance concern when urging rejection of FSD homologation. The permanent removal is simultaneously a regulatory concession and an architectural pivot toward behavior-inference. Critical framing: removing manual speed controls removes a disengagement trigger (owners frustrated by overly cautious speed) but also removes user agency over a core FSD behavior, generating community confusion. This is a software behavior decision — not a v15 milestone — but it affects how all current v14.x and future v15 builds interact with speed compliance.

positive_signals: Removing hard-coded speed offsets addresses a specific regulatory objection raised by Sweden and the EU — may unblock or accelerate EU homologation path
Behavior-inference approach (learning from accelerator taps) is architecturally more sophisticated than manual sliders and aligns with v15 AI-native design philosophy
NotATeslaApp and Teslarati both corroborate Ashok's statement
negative_signals: Decision removes driver control over speed — generates significant owner confusion and frustration per community feedback covered by Teslarati
Incorrect speed-zone data is a documented source of FSD disengagements in many regions; removing user override could increase disengagements until inference model matures
No timeline given for when implied-preference speed learning ships; current v14.3.7 still uses fixed speed behavior

keyChanges.title: Elluswamy posts '10 million robots' correction as Giga Texas factory rises — no production numbers disclosed
keyChanges.description: On July 31, 2026, Tesla Optimus chief Ashok Elluswamy posted a terse 'Correction, 10 million robots' on X, clarifying the long-term annual capacity target for the dedicated Optimus factory under construction at Giga Texas (not the Fremont pilot line, which targets 1M/yr). The post was covered by Teslarati and Basenor. Separately, Basenor published a Giga Texas construction update covering drone footage through July 27, 2026: a multi-story steel superstructure is rising across the 5.2M sq-ft site, seven large cranes operating simultaneously, and floor decking installation is underway — construction pace described as accelerated, not standard commercial build. Context that makes these headlines misleading: (1) Elluswamy's '10M robots' post adds zero new information — Musk cited this figure repeatedly since at least mid-2025; it is a long-term aspirational target for a factory that does not produce a single unit yet; (2) the Giga Texas construction milestone has a volume production target of Summer 2027, not now; (3) no Optimus unit count, production rate, takt time, yield, or Academy delivery total has been disclosed by Tesla since the Q2 earnings call on July 22; (4) the Fremont line status as of week ending August 6 remains 'installing first-generation lines' per Q2 letter language — no official correction to 'production started.' The late-July/August window Musk set on Q1 earnings as the production start target has now elapsed with no official confirmation of first robot output.

Elluswamy's correction reconfirms 10M/yr long-term Texas capacity target, signaling program is intact
Two-site manufacturing strategy (Fremont 1M + Texas 10M) structurally on track from a facilities standpoint

key_metrics.actual: 0 confirmed units produced from Fremont first-gen line; Giga Texas in construction (7 cranes, floor decking installed as of July 27)
key_metrics.target: Fremont: production start late July–August 2026 (Q1 guidance, now elapsed); Giga Texas: volume production Summer 2027; long-term: 1M/yr Fremont + 10M/yr Texas

keyChanges.title: BYD debuts Xiao Di humanoid robot — Optimus competitor commercially deployed while Tesla is still pre-production
keyChanges.description: BYD confirmed and deployed its first humanoid robot, Xiao Di, at its 'Di Space' showroom in Zhengzhou in early August 2026. Multiple sources corroborate the announcement and deployment: TechNode (July 27), kr-asia, The Next Web, Notebookcheck, and Stuff South Africa (August 5 teaser update). Key details: Xiao Di stands 1.61m tall, weighs 58.5kg, has 31 degrees of freedom, and features real-time multilingual translation (6 Chinese dialects + 6 foreign languages), 360-degree vision, and an onboard AI model for object/facial recognition. BYD's plan is to deploy 2-3 units per BYD dealership, with the robot greeting customers and explaining vehicles. BYD made clear this is a fully functional prototype, not a concept. US government is reportedly blocking BYD's access to the US market before the debut. The competitive significance for Optimus: BYD — a company with supply chain scale, actuator sourcing, and manufacturing depth that Tesla explicitly lacks for Optimus — is now commercially deploying a humanoid robot while Tesla cannot confirm a single Fremont Optimus unit has come off the line. Chinese competitors (Unitree G1 at $17,990 on Amazon; BYD Xiao Di for dealerships) are advancing commercial use cases while Tesla is still in 'installing lines' and 'Optimus Academy training data collection' phases.

positive_signals: BYD's entry validates the humanoid robot market opportunity Tesla is targeting
Xiao Di is a limited-use dealership greeter, not a general-purpose factory robot — different use case than Optimus's industrial/household target
US market access reportedly blocked for BYD robot, reducing direct near-term competition on Tesla's home turf
negative_signals: BYD — still behind Tesla in AI but far ahead in supply chain depth and actuator sourcing — is now commercially deploying a humanoid robot while Tesla cannot confirm Fremont production has started
Xiao Di is already working in BYD showrooms; Optimus first builds are still destined for internal Optimus Academy training data collection

BYD's deployment pace (2-3 units per dealership chain-wide) implies meaningful scale faster than Tesla's Academy-first approach

keyChanges.title: Tesla, SpaceX Confirm Terafab Groundbreaking: $16.8B First Phase, 100M Sq Ft, Civil Work Underway
keyChanges.description: On August 6, 2026, Tesla and SpaceX made an official public announcement confirming the Terafab chip manufacturing facility in Grimes County, Texas will proceed with $16.8 billion in first-phase investment. Governor Abbott endorsed the project publicly, and SpaceX representatives met with Grimes County residents on August 5-6, confirming JETI tax agreements are signed/active and civil work and foundation preparation are starting 'almost immediately.' The facility is planned at 100+ million square feet — designed to be 'the largest and most valuable building on Earth by far' (Musk's public statement). The plant will vertically integrate logic, memory, packaging, and testing; employ at least 3,000 people; and supply chips for Tesla Optimus robots, Cybercabs, and SpaceX space-based data centers. Build permits were issued around July 26 (four building permits for the Advanced Technology Chip Fabrication facility), and foundation work (excavation, GeoPiers, gravel base) is visibly progressing. The Texas Enterprise Fund granted $30 million toward the project, and SpaceX paid $10 million to Grimes County satisfying a deal milestone. Total multi-phase project scope remains at ~$119 billion. This marks the transition from political/tax approval track (completed July 21-23 with JETI signing) to active site preparation and early construction.

keyChanges.title: Tesla Semi FSD timeline: 'end of year or early 2027' — explicitly sequenced behind Cybercab
keyChanges.description: On the Q2 earnings call, Musk confirmed FSD for Tesla Semi is targeted for end-2026 or early 2027, but explicitly stated it is deprioritized behind Cybercab commercial deployment and Model 3/Y FSD maturity. The 4680 battery cell yield remains the binding constraint for both Semi and Cybercab production ramp. The Nevada Semi factory (1.7M sq ft, 50k/yr capacity) has been ramping since April 2026. Full-year 2026 Semi deliveries estimated at 5,000-15,000 units. Critical read: this is a commercial trucking FSD story (narrow domain), not consumer autonomy expansion.

Volume production target for Cybercab silently removed from 2026 roadmap

245 Cybercabs staged but not deploying into revenue service — inventory pile building
Phoenix and Las Vegas missed H1 2026 launch target; now 'preparations underway' with no new date

optimus.latestStatus: Fremont first-gen Optimus production lines still being installed as of late July 2026; no official production start confirmed despite late-July/August target window from Q1 earnings having elapsed. Giga Texas dedicated factory construction accelerating (7 cranes, multi-story steel, floor decking through July 27). No unit counts, yield, takt time, or Academy delivery numbers disclosed. V3/Gen 3 still unrevealed. BYD Xiao Di commercially deployed in August while Tesla remains pre-revenue.
optimus.nextMilestone: Official confirmation of first Fremont line robot output and Optimus Academy unit delivery; V3 public reveal (no date set); Giga Texas volume production (Summer 2027 target)
concerns: Late-July/August production start window from Q1 earnings has elapsed with no official start confirmation — silent slip pattern identical to Q2 letter dropping 'volume production in 2026' language
Zero unit counts or production rate disclosures; no third-party verification of any Fremont first-gen output
BYD and Chinese competitors (Unitree, Xpeng) are commercially deploying humanoid robots while Tesla remains in training-data-collection phase
Supply chain remains Tesla's self-described 'hardest challenge' — no updates on progress insourcing critical actuator/reducer components since Q2 call
Chinese supply chain decoupling risk: BOM could increase 2-3x if US-China trade restrictions tighten further

terafab.latestStatus: Terafab groundbreaking confirmed August 6; JETI tax abatements signed and active; civil work and foundation prep underway in Grimes County. First phase $16.8B investment; total project scope ~$119B across four phases. 100+ million sq ft facility targeting 3,000+ jobs and production of logic, memory, and packaging chips for Tesla and SpaceX.
terafab.nextMilestone: Full-scale construction within several months (target Q4 2026 / Q1 2027); tool procurement and installation; process qualification and first-silicon targets unknown but likely 2027-2028 for initial wafer production
concerns: No specific production ramp timeline; pre-production phases (civil, tool install, process qual) expected multi-year
Environmental and community opposition (water usage, noise, identity) remains unresolved despite JETI approval
Supply-chain and workforce recruitment for 3,000+ skilled semiconductor jobs remains unproven
Total investment ($119B) implies high execution risk; cash burn during construction significant
Fab efficiency, yield path, and competitive positioning vs. Samsung/TSMC not yet tested
